tag: Episode 24 · Because There Is No Water
title: Because There Is No Water

beats.t: At dawn, mist lay low along the river. A pink pig slept curled on a wet stone.
A white hair was wound around her foreleg. She'd retied it so often through the night that the knot had three layers.
Found you. You really slept here?
Moka. Where's Yeongnyangi?
Not yet.
Yeoni nodded. The faded white petal on her head sagged with dew.
My lady, let's go inside first. Sleep on cold stones, and Eul Wood takes damage from the roots up.
What would I do inside? If I stay here, I'll see him as soon as he comes back.
Go inside and eat. If the cat sees you like this, he'll get angry at me.
Moka took her by the scruff and tugged. The bookmark ribbon around her injured leg dragged over wet stone.
Mist over the water scattered and gathered again. Between it, one black ripple passed silently. Nobody saw.
A river map Moka had brought from the market lay on the long reading-room table. Only Yeongnyangi's chair at the end was empty.
Let's find his trail first. That's where he last sat.
What's this under the chair? Red powder.
Rust. Smells like rotting metal.
Yeoni swept the powder together with a hoof. A few grains rode the breeze onto a potted plant by the window.
The little tree flinched. One rust-dusted leaf curled yellow and fell onto the table.
Yeoni started to pick it up, then stopped. The white hair around her hoof had red powder on its tip too.
Rust is where metal has been ailing. Mr. Cat must have been in a great deal of pain.
Yundal laid the fallen leaf on his palm. Red stains had spread along its veins.
Just sitting here can do this to a tree?
Metal overcomes Wood. That's why Mr. Cat was always careful beside you, my lady.
Then we were wrong for each other from the start. Yeongnyangi and me.
No. Pass me the kettle, please.
Yundal poured water over the leaf. As the red stain dissolved and ran off, the curled leaf opened a little.
Metal generates Water, and Water nourishes Wood. With water between, metal feeds wood instead of cutting it.
[ Year Stem 壬 · Frozen ]
Your water is Yang Water in your Year Stem. That water is frozen now.
She wetted the rust at the hair's tip with kettle water. It wouldn't dissolve, only clung more tightly.
Why won't this one come off?
Because it's ordinary water. The water that reaches Mr. Cat must flow from within your chart.
What about the pig's fire? You said her fire melts him.
When water flows, fire finds its course too. It eases to the right strength without going out.
A spark jumped from her hoof by itself. The river map's corner blackened.
Pig, don't burn the map. It's our only one.
(Just melt the ice. If my water flows, Yeongnyangi won't melt.)
Yeoni braced herself on the table and stood. Her injured leg throbbed, but she didn't sit back down.
To the vault. My character board's there.
Weren't we looking for the cat?
Both. Even if he comes back, he'll melt again if my water stays frozen.
Fine. But I'm carrying the map.
My lady, forcing that ice to melt hurts. Didn't the tiger say so too?
Then I'll do the hurting. It's the only thing I can do right now.
The three went down to the memory vault. Yeoni's chart floated at its center. Seven of its eight slots were lit.
[ Year 壬午 · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □辰 ]  7/8
The first character, 壬, looked more like a lump of ice than writing. Frozen black, it held something writhing inside.
It was like this when I found it in the library. Something moves inside.
The tiger's water is cold and black. It froze yours.
That striped jerk. Every time we see it, it breaks something else before leaving.
Yundal, step aside.
My lady, wait.
Waiting for the tiger would hurt less. We just don't know when she'll come.
And he keeps melting while we wait. I won't wait.
Yeoni had already raised a hoof. An ember of Byeong Fire formed at its tip.
You melt ice with fire. I've got plenty of fire.
That's the problem!
Flames wrapped around 壬. As white steam rose from the ice, pain cracked through Yeoni's chest.
Ah—it hurts!
She didn't withdraw the fire. Gritting her teeth, she pushed her forelegs farther forward. A thin crack opened in the ice.
Another scene poured through it. Rain was falling; water streamed from the edge of a bus-stop roof.
Someone stood alone in a corner, without an umbrella, wet hair hiding their face.
An umbrella tilted halfway toward that person. The hand holding it was small and familiar. Yeoni's own hand.
One shoulder beneath the umbrella was half-soaked. Yeoni's hand tilted the umbrella farther toward it.
Let's share. Just until the bus comes.
Her own voice. Rain blurred the bus numbers on the sign beyond reading.
Laughter sounded beyond the rain. Warm and a little shy. She couldn't tell whose.
The scene broke off. Yeoni lost her fire. As the steam settled, 壬 was still frozen, the crack darker than before.
What was that? I've never been to that stop.
A scene reflected by the ice. I don't know whose memory it is.
Pig, your nose is bleeding.
Yeoni rubbed their nose. Red stained their hoof. Their chest still throbbed inside.
Melt ice with fire, and the water boils away. It burns up before it can nourish you.
Then what do I have besides fire?
I don't know yet. Ice usually yields easiest to whoever froze it.
That tiger would never do that for us.
Exactly.
The vault grew quiet. A black hairline crack remained, and cold lodged in the same place inside Yeoni's chest would not leave.
By afternoon, she couldn't sit still. Circling the reading room on her injured leg, she hit the table corner three times.
Let's split up. Sitting here is driving me crazy.
All right. I'll take the lower shelves. Plenty of books about water there.
I'll try the market. Ask whether something white, round, rude, and wearing a hat passed by.
I'll take the river. That's where I last saw him.
My lady, meet here before sunset. Today's sky is strange.
Yundal checked the old folding umbrella tied to his bag before pointing outside. The sky cracked yesterday was oddly dark today. A corner of the sun looked bitten away.
What's wrong with the sun? Just like on the festival island.
That's why I'm saying this. Don't stay alone too long.
At the same time, downstream, a white cat sat where the mist was thickest.
Yeongnyangi soaked his rusted paw in the river. Where water touched, rust unraveled like thread and washed away.
Metal generates Water. With water, it needn't be a blade.
The same words Yundal had spoken that morning. Yeongnyangi lifted his paw and studied the dissolved rust for a long time.
Her water is still frozen. Metal cannot melt ice.
Yeongnyangi looked at his reflection in the river. His violet eyes briefly rippled gold, then settled again.
You told me to step aside.
He murmured the words once more, then smiled faintly.
Still, your fire was there. That's a relief.
The river turned black. Dozens of black hands shot from the water at once, exactly where Yeongnyangi's paw had been soaking.
Didst thou long for water, little cat? When thou art weakest, water is nearest.
You. You cracked the library sky.
Thou madest the crack. Brace the sky with a rusted blade, and the sky breaks first.
He stood, a blade rising from his rusted paw. It was half as long as yesterday, rust spreading along its tip.
The blade severed three black hands. They came back as six. Six became twelve.
Metal cleaves to metal. Leave that girl and come unto me.
No. She's my only charge.
One black hand seized Yeongnyangi's scruff. Another his left paw, another his tail. His small body was dragged toward the water.
Yeoni.
Halfway through calling the name, Yeongnyangi closed his mouth. If he called, Yeoni would come. And then that child would stand before these hands.
Without another sound, the white cat was dragged into black water. One great ripple rose, then the river grew impossibly calm.
Nothing remained on the bank. Mist settled again.
At sunset, Moka turned toward the river on the way back from market. Someone had seen a white, round thing heading downstream.
Hey, customer service. I've come to tell on the pig. She cried all night.
No answer. Sniffing, Moka stepped from wet stone to wet stone. The smell of melting metal mingled with an unfamiliar cold scent.
A large palmprint marked the mud beside the water. Much larger than a human hand, its fingers far too long. At its center lay a strand of white fur.
This.
Moka picked up the hair. The same white fur Yeoni wore around her hoof, but colder than the river.
Moka! I went all the way downstream, but nothing—
Yeoni stopped. They saw the white fur in Moka's paw. And the great handprint in the mud beneath it.
Where did you get that?
Pig, sit first. Sit and listen.
Where did you get it?!
Yundal ran up, panting. With his glove off, the hole in his palm swirled on its own, as though something enormous had just passed nearby.
Too late. There were so many of those hands here just now.
[ Hour Stem 庚 · Borrowed slot · Connection lost ]
Something snapped where the cold lodged in Yeoni's chest. Only she heard it.
They took Yeongnyangi.
The sun's last corner was eaten away. A black disk hung over the river. Red light burned in a ring around its rim.
The sun. The sun's gone.
An eclipse. It's finally revealing its body.
The cat is safely received, vessel. An empty sheath happened to be useful.
Give him back. Give Yeongnyangi back!
I shall return him. Come thou instead, an empty vessel.
The black disk slowly blinked, like an eyelid. And every shadow over the river turned toward Yeoni.
